q: Newton was able to point out and express precisely that all bodies in the universe are attracting one another.
e: This is a fundamental premise of Newton's law of gravitation.

q: Gravitational force causes bodies which are above the earth's surface to fall onto the earth's surface.
e: This is a primary effect of the Earth's gravitational force.

q: The gravitational force enables the sun to go round the moon and the earth to go round the sun.
e: The gravitational force enables the moon to go round the earth and the earth to go round the sun.

q: Newton stated the gravitational law as follows: Everybody attracts every other body in the universe.
e: This is the opening statement of Newton's law of gravitation.

q: The gravitational force between two bodies is directly proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
e: This is the exact statement of the inverse square law of gravitation.

q: In symbols, the law of gravitation is expressed as $F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r}$.
e: The correct formula is $F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, as it is an inverse square law.

q: $G$ is a constant which is the same for all bodies in the universe.
e: The universal gravitational constant $G$ does not change depending on the bodies involved.

q: According to experimental measurements, the value of $G$ in the MKS system is found to be $6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ m}^3 \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$.
e: This is the accepted experimental value of the gravitational constant in MKS units.

q: The value of $G$ in the MKS system can also be written as $\text{N m}^2 \text{kg}^{-2}$.
e: This is an equivalent unit representation for the gravitational constant.

q: The attractions of the moon and the sun upon water of the earth cause tides.
e: This is listed as a direct application of Newton's law of gravitation.

q: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the electromagnetic attraction of the earth.
e: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the gravitational attraction of the earth.

q: A unit vector is a vector that has the magnitude 1.
e: This is the standard definition of a unit vector provided in the text.
